headline: Public hearing on proposed zoning changes allowing roof-mounted wind energy systems.
summary: The proposed ordinance would allow roof-mounted wind energy systems as accessory uses in listed zoning districts. It also sets height rules, adds definitions, and excludes these systems from wind energy facility rules.
items: Section 1: Add roof-mounted wind energy systems as a Y (yes) accessory use in the zoning use table for RC, R1, R2, R3, B1, B2, B4, B5, BPD, I, and NRCC districts
Section 2: Allow roof-mounted wind energy systems an extra 5 feet over the maximum building height
Section 3: Add definitions for wind energy, wind energy system, rated nameplate capacity, wind energy system height, and roof-mounted wind energy system
Roof-mounted systems are defined as those rated at 10 kilowatts or less per turbine and up to 20 feet high (corrected from 10 feet)
Section 4: State that roof-mounted wind energy systems are not wind energy facilities under Section 6.9
Ordinance takes effect as provided by city charter
Vote to close the public hearing
Vote to refer the matter to the Planning Board for their recommendation
plain_text:
CITY OF SALEM 
OCTOBER 19, 2026 
JOINT PUBLIC HEARING OF THE  
CITY COUNCIL AND THE PLANNING BOARD 
AMENDED due to correction of ten (10) feet to twenty (20) 
feet 
 
Section 1. Section 3.1 Table of Principal and Accessory is hereby amended by inserting a new use in 
section E. ACCESSORY USES as follows: 
 
Use  RC  R1  R2  R3  B1  B2  B4  B5  BPD  I  NRCC   
Wind Energy System,Roof-Mounted  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y  Y   
Section 2. Section 4.1.2 Notes to Table of Dimensional Requirements is hereby amended by inserting 
the line “and roof-mounted wind energy systems” after “medium-scale ground mounted solar energy 
systems” in subsection 8 and by inserting a new subsection 10:“The limitations on height of buildings 
shall apply to roof-mounted wind energy systems with an additional allowance of 5 feet over the 
maximum height of the building.”Section 3. Section 10.0, "Definitions," is hereby amended by inserting 
the following definitions in alphabetical order:Wind Energy: Energy received from the conversion of wind 
to electricity.Wind Energy System: A device or structural design feature, a substantial purpose of which 
is to provide for the collection, storage, and distribution of wind energy for lighting, space heating or 
cooling, electricity generation, or water heating.Wind Energy System Rated Nameplate Capacity: The 
maximum rated output of electric power production equipment for a Wind Energy System.Wind Energy 
System Height: The height of the Wind Energy System is measured from the base of the system to the 
tip of the blade at its highest point.Wind Energy System, Roof-Mounted: An Active Wind Energy System 
that is structurally mounted to the roof of a building or structure; shall be considered those with a rated 
nameplate capacity less than or equal to 10 kilowatts per turbine, and a height up to twenty (20) 
feet.Section 4. Section 6.9.1, is hereby amended by adding the phrase “Wind Energy System, Roof-
Mounted, as defined in Section 10.0, are not considered wind energy facilities as defined in this section 
(Section 6.9).” at the end of the section, so that it shall read as follows:6.9.1 Purpose. The purpose of 
this section is to accommodate wind energy facilities in appropriate locations, while minimizing any 
adverse visual, safety, and environmental impacts of the facilities. Wind Energy Systems, Roof-
Mounted, as defined in Section 10.0, are not considered wind energy facilities as defined in this section 
(Section 6.9).This ordinance shall take effect as provided by city charter.

“The limitations on height of buildings shall apply to roof-mounted wind energy systems with an 
additional allowance of 5 feet over the maximum height of the building.” 
Section 3. Section 10.0, "Definitions," is hereby amended by inserting the following definitions in 
alphabetical order: 
Wind Energy: Energy received from the conversion of wind to electricity. 
Wind Energy System: A device or structural design feature, a substantial purpose of which is to 
provide for the collection, storage, and distribution of wind energy for lighting, space heating or 
cooling, electricity generation, or water heating. 
Wind Energy System Rated Nameplate Capacity: The maximum rated output of electric power 
production equipment for a Wind Energy System. 
Wind Energy System Height: The height of the Wind Energy System is measured from the base 
of the system to the tip of the blade at its highest point. 
Wind Energy System, Roof-Mounted: An Active Wind Energy System that is structurally 
mounted to the roof of a building or structure; shall be considered those with a rated nameplate 
capacity less than or equal to 10 kilowatts per turbine, and a height up to twenty (20) feet. 
Section 4. Section 6.9.1, is hereby amended by adding the phrase “Wind Energy System, Roof-
Mounted, as defined in Section 10.0, are not considered wind energy facilities as defined in this 
section (Section 6.9).” at the end of the section, so that it shall read as follows: 
6.9.1 Purpose. The purpose of this section is to accommodate wind energy facilities in 
appropriate locations, while minimizing any adverse visual, safety, and environmental impacts of 
the facilities. Wind Energy Systems, Roof-Mounted, as defined in Section 10.0, are not 
considered wind energy facilities as defined in this section (Section 6.9). 
This ordinance shall take effect as provided by city charter.
